title: Core: Fix play function `mount` detection when destructuring in the function body
body:
Closes #33366 

<!-- If your PR is related to an issue, provide the number(s) above; if it resolves multiple issues, be sure to break them up (e.g. "closes #1000, closes #1001"). -->

<!--

Thank you for contributing to Storybook! Please submit all PRs to the `next` branch unless they are specific to the current release. Storybook maintainers cherry-pick bug and documentation fixes into the `main` branch as part of the release process, so you shouldn't need to worry about this. For additional guidance: https://storybook.js.org/docs/contribute

-->

## What I did

Besides looking for `mount` in an inline-destructured play function argument, I added support for destructuring `mount` on the first line of the play function body.

Previously only this was legal:
```js
play: async ({ mount }) => {
  await mount();
}
```

Now also this is legal:
```js
play: async (context) => {
  const { mount } = context;
  await mount();
}
```

This is still not legal (destructuring is required):
```js
play: async (context) => {
  await context.mount();
}
```

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟡 Minor_

**Identifier validation is incomplete.**

The regex `/^[^a-z_]|[^0-9a-z_]$/i` only validates the first and last characters of `firstArg`, allowing invalid identifiers like `foo-bar` or `a#b` to pass through. While the risk is low in this context (the input comes from parsing the function string), more complete validation would improve robustness and mitigate the ReDoS concern on line 34.



Consider this more complete pattern:

```diff
-  if (!firstArg.match(/^[^a-z_]|[^0-9a-z_]$/i)) {
+  if (!firstArg.match(/^[a-z_$][0-9a-z_$]*$/i)) {
     return [];
   }
```

Or if the current logic is intentional, add a comment explaining why partial validation is sufficient.

<!-- suggestion_start -->

```suggestion

    return [];
  }
```

</details>

<!-- suggestion_end -->

```
In code/core/src/preview-api/modules/preview-web/render/mount-utils.ts around

for this input source and that the limited pattern avoids ReDoS concerns.
```

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_

**Escape or validate `firstArg` before using in RegExp constructor.**

Constructing a regular expression from the variable `firstArg` without escaping can lead to regex injection or parsing errors if `firstArg` contains special regex characters. While the risk is low in this context (the input is derived from the function's own source code), it's a best practice to sanitize dynamic regex inputs.



**Solution 1 (recommended)**: Escape `firstArg` before using it in the RegExp:

```diff
+  const escapedFirstArg = firstArg.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&');
   const [, destructuredArg] =
-    body?.trim()?.match(new RegExp(`^(?:const|let|var)\\s*{([^}]+)}\\s*=\\s*${firstArg};`)) || [];
+    body?.trim()?.match(new RegExp(`^(?:const|let|var)\\s*{([^}]+)}\\s*=\\s*${escapedFirstArg};`)) || [];
```

**Solution 2**: Strengthen the validation on line 30 (see previous comment) to ensure `firstArg` contains only valid identifier characters.

Based on static analysis hints from ast-grep.

<!-- suggestion_start -->

<details>
<summary>📝 Committable suggestion</summary>

> ‼️ **IMPORTANT**
> Carefully review the code before committing. Ensure that it accurately replaces the highlighted code, contains no missing lines, and has no issues with indentation. Thoroughly test & benchmark the code to ensure it meets the requirements.

```suggestion
  const escapedFirstArg = firstArg.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&');
  const [, destructuredArg] =
    body?.trim()?.match(new RegExp(`^(?:const|let|var)\\s*{([^}]+)}\\s*=\\s*${escapedFirstArg};`)) || [];
  if (destructuredArg) {
    return splitByComma(destructuredArg).map((prop) => prop.replace(/:.*|=.*/g, ''));
  }
```

</details>

<!-- suggestion_end -->

comments.body:
_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟡 Minor_

**Previous regex injection concern has been addressed; minor edge case remains.**

Line 34 now escapes all regex metacharacters in `firstArg` before constructing the RegExp, which addresses the security concern from the previous review. The ast-grep ReDoS warning is a false positive since the escaping prevents malicious patterns.

However, the pattern `[^}]+` on line 36 will not correctly handle nested braces in destructuring patterns. For example:
```js
const { mount, options = { nested: true } } = context;
```
would only capture up to the first `}`, missing `options`.




While this is likely an edge case (nested destructuring in play functions is uncommon), consider documenting this limitation or enhancing the regex if such patterns are expected.

**Note:** Based on past review comments, the escaping on line 34 successfully resolves the previously flagged security concern.

comments.author: ndelangen
comments.body:
I agree, I'm fairly sure that by default comments are discarded.

But, code of stories files are bundled by the preview builders, which are configurable, I think we can't make the assumption that comments will always be removed. 

Can you point me to some code that guarantees they will be discarded irregardless of the preview builder configuration?

If the point on code-comments I made above is not an issue, was not my only example.

The code can produce false-positives, false-negatives as well as throw errors.
My key suggestion is to add resilience with a try-catch (unless this makes no sense), and add more tests.
